title: One command writes a valid _sources.csv row
goal: A stdlib command takes a url, title, publisher, licence and reuse class (and optional version and artifact hash), writes the row with the id from kbid, converges on a repeated url, and the row passes check.py; kb-add-topic, kb-census, kb-ingest and kb-research use it instead of a hand-written CSV writer

gates.question: Where does the row writer live?
options: a new MCP tool beside the read-only kb_* tools

notes: Baseline census: tool results of 314 transcripts of this project (52 sessions, 262 subagent runs), about 4 characters a token; each result is also re-read from cache on every later turn of its session. 115 ad-hoc Python appends to _sources.csv and 90 ad-hoc reads. kbid.py url only prints the id; rag.py src only reads; ql_research.py write_research appends rows for the query log alone; census.py rewrites the whole table. kb-add-topic/SKILL.md, kb-census/SKILL.md and kb-ingest/SKILL.md tell the agent to append rows with a CSV writer, and check.py rejects bad ids, licences and reuse classes afterwards. Kb facts: public/agents/subagents-vs-deterministic-tools.md:74 (a fixed sequence becomes one tool, DOC S1935), public/agents/agent-evaluation.md:36 (DOC S1935).
